http://mignews.com/news/politic/seul-per.title: Сеул перешел к открытой критике Киева из-за скандала с пленными КНДР - Guardian | MigNews - Новости Израиля и Мира на русском языке
http://mignews.com/news/politic/seul-per.p2: Скандал вокруг двух северокорейских военнопленных превратил осторожную поддержку Украины со стороны Сеула в открытую критику. Об этом 29 сентября написало издание The Guardian в развернутой статье, посвященной дипломатическому скандалу между Украиной и Южной Кореей в связи с разглашением информации о передаче двух северокорейских военнопленных. Анализируя последствия конфликта, издание отмечает, что после того как Россия начала полномасштабное вторжение в Украину, Сеул осудил действия Москвы, присоединился к западным санкциям и в июле пообещал предоставить пакет поддержки в размере 100 миллионов долларов. В то же время страна дистанцировалась от боевых действий, отвергая прямую военную помощь Киеву, следуя своей практике не поставлять летальное оружие странам, находящимся в состоянии войны. До полномасштабного вторжения Россия являлась одним из крупнейших торговых партнеров Южной Кореи. Правительство Ли Чжэ Мена также стремится к тому, чтобы улучшить отношения с Пхеньяном, отметило The Guardian. Конфликт из-за пленных северокорейцев превратил осторожную поддержку Киева в открытую критику - в основном со стороны соратников Ли. Так, Ким Бен Чжу, депутат от Демократической партии, заявил, что нет «ни причин, ни необходимости» поддерживать Украину. Он также призвал правительство «немедленно» пересмотреть вопрос оказания помощи. 23 сентября президент Украины Владимир Зеленский во время Генеральной Ассамблеи ООН заявил, что украинская сторона передала Южной Корее двух военнопленных из КНДР. Он сообщил, что передача двух военнопленных состоялась недавно. 24 сентября президент Южной Кореи Ли Чжэ Мен обвинил Украину в нарушении договоренности о неразглашении после того, как Киев сообщил о передаче Сеулу двух северокорейских военнопленных. Он заявил, что вопрос их репатриации является «чрезвычайно чувствительным» и «связанным с дипломатией и национальной безопасностью». Позже украинские СМИ со ссылкой на источник в Офисе президента сообщили, что украинская сторона отрицает существование соглашения о конфиденциальности с Сеулом. Южнокорейская администрация заявила, что такое отрицание «серьезно подрывает» взаимное доверие и наносит ущерб дружественным отношениям между странами. По заявлению Сеула, украинское правительство само настаивало на конфиденциальности передачи, опасаясь внутренней критики из-за упущенной возможности обменять северокорейских военнопленных на украинских. Сеул согласился на конфиденциальность, принимая во внимание безопасность военнопленных и их семей, а также вопросы дипломатии и безопасности. В то же время представитель администрации президента Южной Кореи заявил, что Зеленский обнародовал информацию о передаче без предварительных разъяснений или консультаций, несмотря на наличие - по утверждению Сеула - взаимной договоренности. Издание Korea JoongAng Daily со ссылкой на высокопоставленного представителя администрации президента Южной Кореи сообщило, что Украина заранее уведомила Южную Корею о планах президента Владимира Зеленского упомянуть двух военнопленных из КНДР во время выступления на Генеральной Ассамблее ООН, несмотря на предварительную договоренность этого не делать. По его словам, украинская сторона уведомила Сеул по дипломатическим каналам и попросила отнестись к этому с пониманием.

https://www.techtimes.com/articles/32822.title: Samsung Foundry 2nm Yield Hits 60%; Chips Still Drain More Power Than Snapdragon
https://www.techtimes.com/articles/32822.p1: Samsung Electronics' foundry division has approached a yield of 60% on its first-generation 2nm Gate-All-Around process, a dramatic climb from below 20% in late 2025 — but industry officials say the harder engineering challenge has already shifted from counting good chips per wafer to proving those chips can meet the power budgets real customers actually specify. Independent device-level testing has reportedly found that Samsung's 2nm chips consume more power than Qualcomm's latest Snapdragon processors in equivalent workloads — a gap that is now the primary reason major customers have not yet committed capacity, and the engineering priority Samsung is racing to close before its Tesla AI6 production ramp is scheduled to begin in 2027.
https://www.techtimes.com/articles/32822.p2: Yield in semiconductor manufacturing is not a single number. The figure approaching 60% that ChosunBiz reported September 28, 2026 is a front-end wafer yield: the fraction of chips on a wafer that pass functional tests before packaging and final processing begin, as SF2 process yield approaching 60% confirmed across multiple industry sources. After back-end processing — dicing, packaging, thermal testing, and final electrical verification — the effective yield of chips that actually reach customers is considerably lower, with industry estimates placing it in the 40% range for Samsung's current 2nm process. That effective yield figure is unlinked here as the specific April 2026 SamMobile source could not be independently confirmed in this session; the claim is corroborated by multiple other outlets.

https://www.albayan.ae/economy/business/.title: ترامب يكشف عن خطة كوريا الجنوبية لاستثمار 54 مليار دولار بمشروع طاقة في ألاسكا
https://www.albayan.ae/economy/business/.p1: يعتزم الرئيس الأمريكي دونالد ترامب إعلان خطط لاستثمار كوريا الجنوبية نحو 54 مليار دولار في مشروع لتصدير الغاز الطبيعي من ألاسكا، وهو مقترح يحظى منذ فترة طويلة بدعم السيناتور الجمهوري دان سوليفان، الذي يخوض هناك سباقاً تنافسياً لإعادة انتخابه. وسيكون هذا الاستثمار المرة الثانية خلال الأسبوع الجاري التي يسعى فيها الرئيس الجمهوري إلى تسليط الضوء على فرص الاستثمار الأجنبي التي أتاحتها السياسة التجارية لإدارته في ولايات يخوض فيها مرشحون جمهوريون لمجلس الشيوخ سباقات انتخابية محتدمة. وكان قد أعلن عن صفقة مماثلة، أول من أمس الاثنين، في المكتب البيضاوي تتعلق بمصنع ضخم للصلب في ولاية آيوا. ويأتي الاستثمار في ألاسكا ضمن تعهدات قطعت في إطار اتفاق تجاري أُبرم مع كوريا الجنوبية عام 2025، وتضمن تعهدات باستثمارات بقيمة 350 مليار دولار في الولايات المتحدة مقابل خفض الرسوم الجمركية الأمريكية على السيارات الكورية الجنوبية وقطع غيار السيارات ومنتجات أخرى. وأكد البيت الأبيض الإعلان اليوم، بعدما أوردته وكالة بلومبرغ للأنباء للمرة الأولى. وشجع سوليفان، الذي كان من أبرز الداعمين لمشروع الغاز الطبيعي في ألاسكا، الاستثمارات الكورية الجنوبية، وهو سيناتور شغل المنصب لفترتين ويواجه منافسة قوية من الديمقراطية ماري بيلتولا، العضوة السابقة في مجلس النواب. وقال البيت الأبيض إن المشروع يتضمن خط أنابيب للغاز الطبيعي بطول 1300 كيلومتر يربط المنحدر الشمالي في ألاسكا بمحطة لتصدير الغاز الطبيعي المسال في جنوب الولاية، وإن المشروع سيؤدي في نهاية المطاف إلى خفض تكاليف الطاقة التي يتكبدها سكان الولاية من خلال توفير إمدادات موثوقة وآمنة.

https://warontherocks.com/rated-ready-is.title: Rated Ready is Not Ready: What America’s Korea Exercises Actually Measure
https://warontherocks.com/rated-ready-is.p1: Join War on the Rocks and gain access to content trusted by policymakers, military leaders, and strategic thinkers worldwide.
https://warontherocks.com/rated-ready-is.p2: “We want to stop the North Koreans as far from Pusan as we can. Block the main road as far north as possible. Contact General Church. If you can’t locate him, go to Taejon and beyond if you can. Sorry I can’t give you more information. That’s all I’ve got. Good luck to you, and God bless you and your men.” -Maj. Gen. William F. Dean, orders to Lt. Col. Charles B. Smith, July 1, 1950, four days before Task Force Smith was overrun at Osan. The battery I served in at Camp Casey, South Korea, the 333rd Field Artillery Target Acquisition Battery, existed to do one thing if North Korea attacked: find the enemy’s guns so our guns could fire back. That was the whole of our unit’s job. I was a private first class and fire support specialist in that battery: the soldier who tells the guns where to shoot. On Nov. 23, 2010, news reached us that North Korea shelled an island called Yeonpyeong, somewhere to the west. That was about all I knew. Our sergeant ordered us to put on armor, go to the armory, and draw live rounds. After drawing ammunition, my squad and I were directed to wait in our Humvee — a task even four junior enlisted men had no trouble executing with minimal direction. That, however, was where our direction ended. No one in that vehicle knew what we were supposed to do next. Nothing in any of the exercises we had done up to that point, which were to prepare us for this exact moment, had given us a next move for that afternoon. So, we stayed where the day had put us: in the motor pool, in the Humvee, waiting. BECOME A MEMBER What Are the Exercises For? 16 years later, the exercises got shorter; Ulchi Freedom Shield, planned for 11 days, ended after only five, following U.S. President Donald Trump’s direction to his defense secretary in a social media post to “substantially reduce” exercises on the Korean Peninsula. The president gave four reasons: his relationship with North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un, the cost, the “hostile” signal the exercises send, and Seoul’s refusal to join America’s military operation to denuclearize Iran. Readiness was not on the list. Retired American and South Korean officers called the cut a blow to readiness, while the Pentagon assured that the move “preserve(s) essential readiness” and resulted in “no degradation to U.S. training objectives.” That assurance applied only to American training objectives — what constitutes “essential” readiness remains undefined. Neither claim can be checked because the readiness the critics invoke and the training objectives the Pentagon cites have never been publicly disclosed. The wider implications of the cut for the alliance are a separate question, but what Washington and Seoul ought to be asking at this juncture is far narrower: What are these exercises actually for? The alliance has one public answer to that question, but it sits at the top of the chain. Both governments state openly that the command post exercise certifies whether a future combined command under a South Korean four-star can meet the conditions for taking wartime operational control — an assessment that was underway in this year’s exercise when the president halved it, with Seoul pressing for a transfer decision at October’s Security Consultative Meeting . South Korea’s defense minister, Ahn Gyu-back, told the National Assembly that the evaluation, including the counterfire portion, finished within the five days that it ran — analysts in Seoul counter that a halved exercise narrows the basis for judging the command Seoul proposes to lead. No outsider can score that dispute either — the communiqués state that “all assessment tasks met the criteria” without listing any tasks, naming any formation, or showing any criteria. The alliance certifies publicly and grades privately. It is hard for me to say the exercises of 2010 produced “readiness.” What they produced, at my level, was a private in a motor pool with live rounds and no idea what to do. Perhaps I was too junior to see the plan; perhaps Private Hoffman was failing to meet the standard; or perhaps the exercises today produce something different — I cannot say, and neither can anything in the public record. If these are rehearsals for war, the alliance can show it without declassifying a page: which units rehearse which wartime missions, in which exercise, graded by whom. The grades can stay classified, and so can the passing mark, but the syllabus cannot. Training the Headquarters, Not the Field Exercise Team Spirit put 200,000 troops in the field at its peak and ended in 1993. The surviving line —Ulchi Focus Lens, then Ulchi Freedom Guardian, now Ulchi Freedom Shield — has been a command post exercise since 1976.  Robert Collins, former chief of strategy for Combined Forces Command, described Key Resolve, Ulchi’s spring counterpart, as being intended to “train staff instead of field units.” Team Spirit trained the field, and its survivors train the command post. The exercise both sides are now arguing over is a staff exercise with field events attached. In August 2010, the Ulchi Freedom Guardian I was in ran with 30,000 American and 56,000 South Korean participants — the Army called it the world’s largest annual command post exercise. My squad’s piece of it was in a bunker at Camp Red Cloud, where we ran 12-hour shifts watching terminals inside a theater-level wargame. Nothing in that week trained the task my squad existed to perform. I am not calling the week worthless, but it was a headquarters exercise doing headquarters training: Four junior enlisted combat arms soldiers were furniture in it. Collins’ view of the spring exercise came from the Chief of Strategy’s office, and my view in August looked the same from the bunker. Ulchi Freedom Shield runs in two phases, defense and then counterattack — the president’s directive cut the counterattack phase, planned for Aug. 24 to 27. The field training scheduled alongside the command post exercise took its own cut: The allies halved those events from fourteen to seven, deferring the rest or converting them to simulations. This year’s exercise involved about 18,000 South Korean troops and an unspecified number of Americans. Defense Minister Ahn says 159 field training exercises remain on this year’s calendar. That the soldiers on the peninsula train at volume is not in question. What is in question is whether that volume trains them for the fight they would actually find themselves in. The Day the Exercises Mattered At 2:34 p.m. on Nov. 23, 2010, the alliance came as close to that fight as it had been in 60 years when a North Korean multiple rocket launcher battery south of the village of Kaun-gol fired a barrage of 170 rounds onto Yeonpyeong Island. The island’s Firefinder counter-battery radar, the same model my battery fielded at Camp Casey, was down with an unknown fault. The fire control center could not locate the launchers. The South Korean Marine artillery crews, with most of their guns ready, executed pre-planned counter-battery fire: Only after the radar came back online could they find and engage the rocket battery. The attack killed two marines and two civilians. Yeonpyeong lies about 125 kilometers west-southwest of Camp Casey. The battery that responded was South Korean by design: Peacetime operational control of South Korean forces returned to Seoul in December 1994. And the intended American response was to hold fire — which is what we did in that motor pool. But the fight was a counterfire fight, and my battery was built around the exact radar that went down on Yeonpyeong. Maybe we had a useful task that afternoon, or maybe we had none. That judgment lived echelons above me, and I cannot make it. But the confusion at my level wasn’t in the waiting. We knew our equipment and our basic combat tasks: Every field exercise we had run tested one or the other. What nothing had taught us was how we were intended to apply that training if North Korea attacked. Army doctrine has held since 1993 that a commander’s intent must be understood two echelons down, so that a unit can act when orders stop. That is the Army’s standard, and it is the only one I measure that afternoon against. The obvious reply is that command post exercises never claimed to be for junior soldiers, so of course a private saw nothing of his job in them. But training the headquarters and training the field are not either-or, and the Army was proving it at the time in two wars at once. The National Training Center put whole brigades, squads to staffs, into one simulated fight, with every echelon evaluated against its mission-essential tasks. I went through it as a specialist, still junior enlisted, before Afghanistan, and left with a working idea of what was expected of me when orders ran out. The command posts got their training in the same rotation — nobody had to choose. Readiness includes the warfighters expected to do the fighting knowing, at least in outline, what they will be asked to do. It also includes the taxpayers who fund the training, and the committees that oversee it, being able to learn what it is for. If a private’s wartime task in Korea is to wait for orders, fine. Then train soldiers to expect it and say so the next time someone defends an exercise as readiness. If standby is the design, it is fair to ask, before anyone mourns or celebrates this cut, why thousands of troops are counted as participants, how many of them are training their actual wartime tasks, and whether the format ever needed the scale both sides are fighting over. Rated Ready Is Not Ready Within weeks of the 2010 shelling, Seoul announced Firefinder radars for the border islands and, within a year, reinforced Yeonpyeong’s garrison. The American side replaced its Firefinders too. Every asset-level fix is documented, and anyone can check it. The same cannot be said for training. Camp Casey’s own release says its ammunition-upload and alert drills are designed to “test the brigade’s ability to rapidly mobilize and deploy.” I went looking for the rest. The closest the public record comes is U.S. Forces Korea’s own exercise instruction, which states a grading system exists for seven mission-essential tasks and monthly readiness assessments. The seven tasks are not listed, nor does anything in the public record state what qualifies as “readiness.”  Whether that means being prepared for a North Korean thrust across the Demilitarized Zone or, as in 2010, refreshing basic skills with no scenario attached, nothing in the open source can say. Descriptive material on the exercises is plentiful — press releases, hearings, and posture statements — what is lacking is any information about what these exercises actually measure below the headquarters. Other theaters publish more. Pacific Command certifies the First Marine Expeditionary Force as a joint task force in print during Balikatan. Japan’s Joint Staff publishes a 10-item list of what its combined exercise with American forces will train. The Army even publishes its mission-essential task standards outright. Korea publishes the least: An instruction with no formation and no task attached. No exercise anywhere puts those pieces together — the formation, the task, and the standard it is judged against. Washington has spent nearly 50 years asking what its exercises accomplish. In 1979, congressional auditors found exercise objectives lacked “meaningful criteria against which to measure accomplishment.” In 2017, the Government Accountability Office conceded the return on exercises resists measurement and may take years to recognize. The alliance ran a version of this year’s experiment in 2018, when the Ulchi Freedom Guardian was suspended outright in favor of reshaped command post training. Gen. Robert Abrams, then the nominee to command U.S. Forces Korea, told the Senate there was “certainly degradation to the readiness of the force,” then called it “slight.” Secretary of Defense James Mattis kept slight the next day and added that there was “nothing significant to it.” Eight months later, in command, Abrams said combined training and readiness “haven’t slowed down one bit,” citing more than a hundred exercises run since January — a recovery possible only on paper, and only because the measure on offer was a count of exercises rather than anything measured in the field. The Army learned the cost of that arithmetic in the Korean War. In July 1950, Gen. Dean directed Task Force Smith to blunt the North Korean thrust at Osan: Most of Col. Smith’s soldiers, like my squad 60 years later, were young and combat-inexperienced. Also like us, they had been rated ready by the Army’s evaluation. North Korean forces overran the unit in seven hours. Rated ready and ready are different standards. The Army has known this for 76 years. Measure What Matters I cannot say whether theater-specific training would have helped the soldiers of Task Force Smith, nor can I say if additional guidance would have saved lives. What I can say is that the threadbare orders Col. Smith received days before his soldiers were sent into combat mirror the level of awareness we had the day we were ordered to draw live rounds and wait. Washington and Seoul, through the Security Consultative Meeting , should direct their joint chiefs’ Military Committee and the combined command to publish the syllabus: which formations own which wartime missions, which exercise trains each, and who certifies the result. The criteria and the grades can stay classified, but the soldier should get the rest of it, his own task in full, and none of that ever has to leave his unit. One may object that the theaters that publish more train at a distance from the adversary, while the alliance’s wartime missions begin inside North Korean artillery range, but both Washington and Seoul have already judged it safe to disclose mission ownership. The 210th Field Artillery Brigade, my former brigade in Korea, publicized its deep-strike mission on U.S. Army Pacific’s Facebook page last year. Seoul’s defense ministry identifies the Ground Operations Command’s counterfire headquarters as responsible for targeting the North’s long-range artillery. A staff officer may object that linking those missions to an exercise calendar would tell Pyongyang who rehearses what and when. Yet both governments already announce each exercise, as the U.S. Forces Korea spokesman put it this August, “to the entire world before it even starts.” Congress, for its part, should attach a reporting requirement to the transfer of command itself. Before wartime operational control passes to a South Korean four-star, the commander of U.S. Forces Korea should report to the defense committees which wartime tasks the assessment measured, which exercises measured them, and how the command graded the result: The Comptroller General should review that report against the missions each formation would own under the new command, and keep reviewing it each year after, as it does now for the F-35. The yardstick already exists: U.S. Forces Korea wrote it into its own exercise instruction, and while the device is not perfect, Congress already uses it across domains. A member who believes the cut damaged readiness needs the review to prove it, and a member who believes the Pentagon’s no-degradation claim needs it just as much. So too does a member who wants the operational control transfer to happen on time — a certification no outsider can check is the easiest kind to hold up. That would close a loop opened in 1979, when the auditors asked for readiness measures built into the exercise program and the Pentagon answered that readiness could not be quantified. 47 years is a long enough wait to give it another try. When I was stationed at Camp Casey, we jokingly called ourselves the speed bumps. Even at the lowest levels of the force, we understood that our role in a Korean contingency, much like Task Force Smith before us, was to sell our lives as expensively as possible to buy the rest of the force time. Every soldier in America’s Korean footprint knows they may be asked to do what the soldiers of 1950 were asked to do. If they are asked again, the Army should be able to give them more than Gen. Dean could give Col. Smith. That begins with training, with a published standard commanders are accountable to, and with the alliance answering what these exercises are actually for. https://www.rondoniadinamica.com/noticia.p1: O Ministério da Defesa da Coreia do Norte condenou nesta quarta-feira (16) um acordo entre Estados Unidos e Coreia do Sul para ampliar o compartilhamento de informações e os exercícios militares conjuntos. O pacto de resposta a possíveis ataques com armas de destruição em massa firmado pelas duas nações é uma “declaração explícita de confronto”, de acordo com Pyongyan. Segundo o governo norte-coreano, o acordo pressupõe o uso de armas nucleares, biológicas e químicas contra a Coreia do Norte em uma eventual crise na Península Coreana. Para Pyongyang, a medida aumenta o risco de emprego de armas de destruição em massa na região. Autoridades de defesa dos EUA e da Coreia do Sul se reuniram em Seul na semana passada para discutir formas de responder às ameaças representadas pelo programa nuclear norte-coreano. A reunião foi conduzida por Woo Kyung-suk, diretor-geral do departamento de planejamento de políticas do Ministério da Defesa sul-coreano, e Jason Hamm, vice-secretário-assistente de Defesa dos EUA para políticas de dissuasão nuclear. Segundo os governos, os programas bélicos da Coreia do Norte contribuem para a instabilidade na Península Coreana e em outras partes da região. https://tidende.dk/ind-og-udland/udland/.title: Nordkorea dømt til at betale Sydkorea for sprængt fælleskontor
https://tidende.dk/ind-og-udland/udland/.p1: I 2018 etablerede Nord- og Sydkorea et kontor, der skulle forbedre deres forhold. Det blev ødelagt i 2020.
https://tidende.dk/ind-og-udland/udland/.p2: Det fremgår af en kendelse, som en domstol i Sydkoreas hovedstad, Seoul, har afsagt onsdag. - Domstolen har afgjort, at Nordkorea skal betale den sydkoreanske regering 44,6 milliarder won i erstatning, siger en talskvinde fra Seoul Central District Court. Beløbet svarer til cirka 210 millioner kroner. Nordkorea har ikke umiddelbart kommenteret afgørelsen. Eksperter vurderer det som usandsynligt, at Nordkorea nogensinde vil betale erstatningen. Det såkaldte forbindelseskontor blev åbnet i 2018 i det tidligere fælles industriområde Kaesong, som ligger nord for den demilitariserede zone, der adskiller de to lande. Nordkorea sprængte bygningen i luften i juni 2020 efter flere dage med stigende spændinger mellem landene. Sydkoreas regering anlagde sagen i 2023 under den daværende sydkoreanske præsident Yoon Suk-yeols regering, som førte en hård linje over for Nordkorea. Yoon Suk-yeol blev afsat i december 2024 efter en kontroversiel beslutning om at indføre militær undtagelsestilstand. Ifølge sydkoreanske medier er det første gang, at Sydkoreas regering gennem et søgsmål har krævet en erstatning fra Nordkorea. Sydkoreas præsident, Lee Jae-myung, der tiltrådte sidste år, har lovet at forbedre det anspændte forhold til nabolandet mod nord. Nordkorea invaderede Sydkorea i 1950 og startede Koreakrigen. I 1953 indgik de to lande en våbenhvile. Våbenhvilen har dog aldrig ført en reel fredsaftale med sig. Nordkorea har de senere år været stærkt kritisk over for årlige militærøvelser, som Sydkorea har afholdt sammen med USA siden 1953. Nordkorea ser det som en stærk provokation, som øger spændingerne på den koreanske halvø. For nylig fik den nordkoreanske melding USA's præsident, Donald Trump, til at forkorte dette års øvelser. RITZAU/AFP

See the Full Data Behind This Forecast - Get a Free Sample Report : Where the Technology Is Heading: AI Moves Into the Scanner Itself The most significant shift in diagnostic imaging is not happening after the scan - it is happening during it. Major manufacturers are embedding deep learning reconstruction (DLR) algorithms directly into image acquisition pipelines, clearing signal-level noise as data is captured rather than cleaning up images afterward. The clinical impact is measurable. GE HealthCare's Sonic DL sequence now enables complex multi-sequence brain and joint MRI protocols to complete in under 15 minutes, allowing hospitals to increase daily throughput per scanner substantially without new capital equipment. Radiology remains the leading specialty for AI-enabled device clearances, with more than 1,100 cleared by the U.S. FDA to date. Alongside this, cloud-native PACS and teleradiology platforms are replacing on-premise image archives, enabling remote reads across multi-site networks and reducing reporting turnaround times. Photon-counting CT and hybrid imaging systems are pushing resolution higher while lowering radiation dose, supporting earlier detection in oncology, cardiology, and neurology. What's Fueling Growth in the Diagnostic Imaging Market AI-Enabled Imaging Adoption: AI-based systems are improving diagnostic precision, shortening scan-to-diagnosis time, and raising patient throughput across care settings. Cloud PACS and Teleradiology Expansion: Remote reading platforms are accelerating reporting and improving specialist access across distributed hospital networks. Photon-Counting CT Commercialization: Ultra-high-definition imaging with reduced radiation exposure is shortening replacement cycles for high-end equipment. Portable and Handheld Imaging: Point-of-care ultrasound and mobile systems are expanding diagnostic access in emergency departments, outpatient centers, and rural facilities. Safer Contrast Agents: Non-nephrotoxic imaging options are extending diagnostic access to chronic kidney disease patients. Certified Refurbished Systems: Lower capital barriers are enabling imaging infrastructure expansion across developing markets. Need Data Specific to Your Region or Segment? Request a Custom Report Challenges Facing the Diagnostic Imaging Market Reimbursement compression is emerging as the sector's most pressing operational constraint. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services introduced an efficiency adjustment in the 2026 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule that permanently reduces work relative value units by 2.5% across roughly 7,700 diagnostic and procedural codes. New combined head and neck CTA codes have produced global payment reductions of up to 30.8%. The result is a growing misalignment between what providers invest in premium scanners and what public payers reimburse - pushing many networks to extend equipment life cycles rather than upgrade. Beyond reimbursement, high acquisition and maintenance costs for MRI and CT systems remain a barrier for community hospitals and providers in developing markets. A persistent shortage of qualified radiologists is contributing to reporting backlogs, while the shift to cloud-based imaging raises data security and cybersecurity considerations for healthcare providers. Recent Strategic Developments in the Diagnostic Imaging Market In May 2026, GE HealthCare introduced next-generation SIGNA MRI technologies and AI-based workflow solutions at ISMRM 2026, including new 3T and helium-free MRI systems, deep learning imaging technologies, and cloud-based research tools. Also in May 2026, Siemens Healthineers launched an integrated workflow solution for CT-guided percutaneous coronary interventions, combining CT imaging, plaque analysis, procedural planning, and cath lab guidance in a single application. In March 2026, Samsung Medison consolidated its U.S. medical imaging divisions, NeuroLogica and Boston Imaging, under the Samsung HME America brand, expanding into AI ultrasound, digital radiography, portable CT, and photon-counting detector technologies. In February 2026, Fujifilm Holdings launched the ARIETTA Deep Insight x ultrasound platform, applying AI and deep learning to improve image quality, with automated workflow tools and real-time virtual sonography. http://www.glas-javnosti.rs/vesti/svet/k.title: Kim Jo Džong odbacila zahteveIAEA: Status Severne Koreje kao nuklearne države „apsolutan”.
http://www.glas-javnosti.rs/vesti/svet/k.p1: Kim Jo Džong, uticajna sestra severnokorejskog lidera Kim Džong Una, odbacila je danas međunarodne pozive Pjongjangu da odustane od nuklearnog programa, poručivši da je status Severne Koreje kao nuklearne države „apsolutan”. „Realnost u kojoj je nuklearni status DNR Koreje trajno utvrđen fizički i pravno ne može se promeniti ni najmanje”, navela je Kim Jo-džong u saopštenju koje je objavila severnokorejska državna novinska agencija KCNA. To je njen odgovor na 70. redovno zasedanje Generalne konferencije Međunarodne agencije za atomsku energiju (IAEA) U Beču gde je izražena zabrinutost zbog širenja severnokorejskih nuklearnih kapaciteta i upućen poziv Pjongjangu da potpuno, proverljivo i nepovratno napusti program nuklearnog naoružanja, u skladu sa Ugovorom o neširenju nuklearnog oružja, prenosi Jonhap. Južna Koreja istražuje ko će naslediti Kim Džong Una u Severnoj Koreji, ćerka ili sin kog možda ima Kim Jo Džong smatra da su pozivi za denuklearizaciju „samo buka” i da nisu ni iznenađujući ni novi. „Bez obzira na to koliko očajnički IAEA i Zapad održavaju periodične sastanke i govore o denuklearizaciji prema unapred utvrđenom scenariju, oni ne mogu da utiču na volju i sposobnost Demokratske Narodne Republike Koreje da preduzme sve neophodne mere za odbranu najviših interesa države”, navela je Kim Jo Džong. Severna Koreja godinama razvija nuklearni i raketni program, uprkos međunarodnim sankcijama i pozivima da odustane od nuklearnog naoružanja. https://www.hani.co.kr/arti/english_edit.p1: Ahead of Chuseok, Korea’s biggest national holiday, the Korean Red Cross met elderly Koreans separated from family members by the Korean War. On Monday, the Korean Red Cross sought out 15 elderly Koreans who have gone decades without a chance to see their family members for the holidays. The organization checked on their well-being, allowed them to share how much they long for their loved ones, and consoled them on the pain of separation. Kim Suk-gyeong, 83, spoke to the Hankyoreh in Seoul’s Seodaemun District. https://www.hani.co.kr/arti/english_edit.p2: The last contact from him was a letter to her mother in 1949. He wrote, “I’ll explain everything when we meet in person. Please take good care of yourselves.” Many separated family members still harbor hopes of being reunited, but their advanced age means time is running out to confirm if their loved ones are still alive and to arrange reunions. https://www.munhwa.com:443/article/11618.p1: 2008년 2월 미국이 시리아 원자로 폭격 관련 비밀 정보를 한국 측에 전달해온 적이 있다. 당시 방한한 크리스토퍼 힐 국무부 동아태 차관보는 물러나는 노무현 정부와 곧 출범할 이명박 정부의 외교안보팀을 각각 만나 “2007년 9월 이스라엘이 폭격한 시리아의 원자로는 북한 영변 원자로와 닮은꼴이며 북한 기술로 지어졌다”고 밝혔다. 미국이 한국의 정권 교체기에 북·시리아 핵 커넥션을 알린 것은 북핵의 제3국 유출에 따른 대북 압박 공조를 위한 행보로 보인다. 당시 문화일보가 이를 보도하자 미국 측이 한국 측에 민감 정보 유출을 항의한 것으로 알려졌다.
https://www.munhwa.com:443/article/11618.p2: 흥미로운 것은 시리아·북한의 무반응이었다. 시리아 정부는 이스라엘의 폭격을 당하고도 침묵했고, 폭격 현장까지 깨끗이 치웠다. 북한도 모르쇠로 일관해 이스라엘의 시리아 폭격은 국제적으로 논란이 되지 않았다. 이후 워싱턴포스트는 2011년 국제원자력기구(IAEA)의 내부 보고서를 인용해 ‘이스라엘이 폭격한 알키바르 원자로는 핵무기 제조용 비밀 시설이었을 가능성이 크다’고 보도해 관심을 끌었는데 이스라엘이 공식 인정한 것은 그로부터 7년 후다. 이스라엘군은 시리아 데이르에조르주(州) 알키바르에 건설 중이던 비밀 원자로를 제거하기 위해 공군 전폭기를 동원해 2007년 9월 ‘오차드 작전’을 벌였다고 인정하며 영상도 함께 공개했다. 파괴된 원자로는 영변의 5㎿ 원자로 복제판 같다.

https://news.webindia123.com/news/Articl.title: North Korea fires additional projectile after short-range ballistic missile launch: South Korea Military
https://news.webindia123.com/news/Articl.p1: According to details shared by South Koreas Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) and reported by Yonhap News Agency, specific parameters regarding the second missile launch were not immediately available as intelligence authorities continued their analysis. The initial provocation occurred around 3:00 p.m. when the JCS detected a short-range ballistic missile fired from the Wonsan area. The missile travelled approximately 450 kilometres before falling into the sea. "We are closely monitoring North Korea's various activities and maintain the capability and readiness to overwhelmingly respond to any provocations, under the staunch South Korea-US combined defence posture," the JCS said in a statement carried by Yonhap News Agency. South Korean and U.S. intelligence tracked the launch from its earliest stages and shared real-time tracking data with Japanese authorities. Following the back-to-back launches, South Korea's National Security Office (NSO) convened an emergency meeting alongside the Ministry of National Defence and the JCS to assess the security situation and evaluate appropriate countermeasures. The NSO condemned the launches as clear violations of U.N. Security Council resolutions and urged Pyongyang to cease military provocations immediately. Sunday's firing comes nine days after Pyongyang launched multiple short-range ballistic missiles from the same region on Sept. 12. State media later confirmed those tests involved tactical cruise missiles, attack drones, and 600-millimetre super-large multiple rocket launchers. The fresh missile tests follow sharp warnings from senior North Korean leadership against U.S.-led joint military manoeuvres in the region. Kim Yo-jong, the influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, recently issued a scathing rebuke of the multinational Pacific Vanguard maritime exercise, vowing that Pyongyang would respond in a "more offensive manner." North Korean state organs have similarly condemned the bilateral South Korea-US Ulchi Freedom Shield and the trilateral Freedom Edge exercises involving Japan, routinely characterising them as rehearsals for an invasion. As reported by Yonhap News Agency, military analysts suspect the first projectile fired on Sunday was a Hwasong-11 series short-range ballistic missile, with detailed evaluations ongoing to determine the specific class of the second projectile. https://www.alanba.com.kw/1377436.p1: طالبت الولايات المتحدة واليابان وكوريا الجنوبية أمس بتعزيز مرونة إمدادات الطاقة الإقليمية بما في ذلك «زيادة مخزونات النفط وتشجيع التعاون بين الدول المنتجة والمستهلكة». جاء ذلك في بيان مشترك صدر عقب اجتماع وزراء خارجية الولايات المتحدة ماركو روبيو واليابان موتيجي توشيميتسو وكوريا الجنوبية تشو هيون على هامش اجتماعات الأسبوع رفيعة المستوى في الجمعية العامة للأمم المتحدة بنيويورك. وشدد الوزراء الثلاثة في بيان مشترك على التزام بلدانهم بإخلاء كوريا الشمالية تماما من الأسلحة النووية وحظر دعم توليد الإيرادات المالية لبرامج كوريا الشمالية النووية وبرامج الصواريخ الباليستية وذلك وفقا لقرارات مجلس الأمن الدولي ذات الصلة مع التأكيد على أن «باب الحوار لا يزال مفتوحا». ودعوا بيونغ يانغ إلى «استئناف الحوار مع مواصلة الجهود الرامية إلى تعزيز السلام والاستقرار في شبه الجزيرة الكورية». وفيما يتعلق بتعزيز الأمن الاقتصادي أكدوا عزم حكوماتهم «على الحفاظ على تجارة حرة وشفافة وتأمين سلاسل التوريد الحيوية». وشددوا على «ضرورة تعزيز مرونة إمدادات الطاقة الإقليمية بما في ذلك زيادة مخزونات النفط وتشجيع التعاون بين الدول المنتجة والمستهلكة». ورحبوا بالمبادرات الإقليمية مثل «مبادرة اليابان (باور آسيا) وجهود جمهورية كوريا لتعزيز أمن الطاقة من خلال التعاون الإقليمي». وأكدوا عزمهم على «تعزيز منظومات التكنولوجيا المتقدمة ومرونة سلاسل التوريد بشكل تعاوني» بالإضافة الى تعزيز وحماية التقنيات الحيوية والناشئة مثل الذكاء الاصطناعي وتكنولوجيا الكم والبنية التحتية الرقمية والتكنولوجيا الحيوية. وعلى صعيد آخر شددوا على التزامهم بتعاون أمني قوي ونؤكد بهذه المناسبة على أهمية الحفاظ على السلام والاستقرار في مضيق تايوان. وجددوا موقفهم الداعم لإيجاد حل سلمي للقضايا المتعلقة بالمضيق ومعارضتهم لأي محاولات لتغيير الوضع الراهن من جانب واحد.

https://www.etnews.com/20260922000434.p1: 바이오모아메디칼(대표 이동한 )이 세계적인 니치 향수·뷰티 박람회인 '피티 프라그란체(Pitti Fragranze) 2026' 참가를 계기로 K-뷰티 브랜드의 유럽 시장 공략에 본격적으로 나선다. 바이오모아메디칼은 지난 11일부터 13일까지 이탈리아 피렌체 스타치오네 레오폴다에서 열린 피티 프라그란체 2026에 참가해 자사 브랜드 '프롬더스킨'을 선보이며 유럽 시장에서 브랜드 인지도를 높였다. 올해 24회째를 맞은 피티 프라그란체에는 니치 향수와 인디 스킨케어 브랜드 등 290여개 브랜드가 참가했으며, 2200명 이상 방문객과 해외 바이어, 약 460명 미디어 관계자가 현장을 찾았다.
https://www.etnews.com/20260922000434.p2: 바이오모아메디칼은 이번 전시에서 지난해에 이어 마련된 인디 스킨케어 전용 섹션 'Soul and Skin'에 참여했다. 'Soul and Skin'은 아방가르드 콘셉트의 인디 스킨케어 브랜드를 소개하는 공간으로, 프롬더스킨은 페이스 및 바디 코스메틱 분야에서 국내 브랜드로는 유일하게 참가해 브랜드와 제품을 알렸다. K-뷰티에 대한 글로벌 관심이 높아지는 가운데 한국콘텐츠진흥원(KOCCA)과 협력해 처음 마련된 특별 공간 'Code Korea @ Fragranze'에도 국내 브랜드들이 참여하면서 한국 뷰티 브랜드에 대한 현지 관심을 확인하는 계기가 됐다. 해당 공간에는 한국콘텐츠진흥원이 선정한 K-뷰티 4개 브랜드가 참여했다. 바이오모아메디칼은 전시 참가에 그치지 않고 현지 네트워크 확대에도 나섰다. 전시 첫날인 11일에는 이탈리아 호스피탈리티 그룹 Soges Group S.p.A.-Place of Charme와 협업해 피렌체 중심가 아르노 강변의 럭셔리 베뉴인 Palazzo Alfieri에서 프롬더스킨 VIP 행사를 개최했다. 이번 행사에는 주요 미디어와 뷰티 인플루언서 등이 참석했으며, 프롬더스킨 제품과 브랜드 철학을 경험할 수 있는 '프롬더스킨 루틴'을 선보였다. 해당 VIP 행사는 오는 10월 9일과 23일에도 추가로 진행될 예정이다. 바이오모아메디칼은 이탈리아 밀라노 지역 고급 에스테틱을 중심으로 프롬더스킨 유통망을 확대하고 있다. 이를 기반으로 현지 프리미엄 뷰티 시장에서 브랜드 입지를 강화하고 유럽 시장 전반으로 사업 영역을 넓힌다는 계획이다. 유럽 시장 진출을 위한 준비도 일찌감치 진행해왔다. 바이오모아메디칼은 회사 설립 첫해인 2023년 11월 유럽 화장품 시장 진출에 필요한 CPNP 등록을 완료했으며, 이번 피티 프라그란체 참가를 계기로 올해 4분기부터 프롬더스킨의 유럽 시장 진출을 더욱 가속화한다는 방침이다. 이동한 바이오모아메디칼 대표는 “회사 설립 첫해인 2023년 11월에 이미 유럽 진출의 필수 관문인 CPNP 등록을 완료했다”며 “이번 피티 프라그란체 참가를 계기로 4분기부터 프롬더스킨의 유럽 진출을 가속화하겠다”고 말했다. 바이오모아메디칼은 이번 피티 프라그란체를 통해 글로벌 니치 향수·뷰티 시장에서 프롬더스킨의 경쟁력을 알리는 동시에 현지 미디어와 인플루언서, 유통 관계자들과의 접점을 확대했다. 향후 이탈리아를 거점으로 유럽 내 유통망을 지속적으로 확대하며 K-뷰티의 유럽 시장 진출을 본격화할 계획이다. 김현민 기자 minkim@etnews.com

https://aninews.in/news/business/china82.p2: Seoul [South Korea], September 22 (ANI): China’s ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) commenced commercial output on its fifth-generation platform, consolidating its market position against entrenched global competitors Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, and Micron, according to a news report by The Korea Herald. The Chinese semiconductor firm also prepares an experimental research facility in Beijing to evaluate an expansion into NAND flash memory, according to a news report by The Korea Herald. Gross die count reflects the aggregate quantity of potential chips extracted from a single wafer before defect screening, rather than an outright gain in production yields. The manufacturing rollout follows CXMT’s rise to fourth place globally in the DRAM sector, capturing 9.5 per cent of second-quarter revenue, according to TrendForce data cited in the report. Market leader Samsung held 39.4 per cent, followed by SK hynix at 24.9 per cent and Micron at 23.3 per cent. Through quadruple patterning techniques, CXMT narrowed the active-area half-pitch in its memory array to 11.95 nanometers, a metric specific to internal array layout that does not directly match node designations used by competitors. Assessing the competitive landscape during an industry webinar in August, TechInsights Vice President and memory-chip analyst Choi Jung-dong noted the gap between CXMT and dominant fabricators.

https://news.webindia123.com/news/Articl.p1: The Chinese semiconductor firm also prepares an experimental research facility in Beijing to evaluate an expansion into NAND flash memory, according to a news report by The Korea Herald. CXMT confirmed that its G5 architecture entered volume production alongside two 24-gigabit LPDDR5X components intended for portable hardware and smartphones. Dynamic random-access memory provides real-time workspace for processors, serving as an essential building block across personal computers, enterprise servers, and mobile devices. The chipmaker reported that the new platform delivers at least 50 per cent more gross dies per wafer compared to its previous process on an 8-gigabit-equivalent standard. Analyzing broader dynamics, an industry official highlighted the pressure building against dominant Korean manufacturers. Chinese memory makers still have a clear cost disadvantage to their Korean rivals, but tight supply has given them more room to win orders and expand production, the news report quoted an industry official. AI 모델도 미국을 바짝 따라붙었다. 두 나라의 패권 다툼은 앞으로 여러 분야로 번질 전망이다. 중국과 바다 하나를 사이에 둔 미국의 동맹국 한국은 고민이 깊을 수밖에 없다. 답을 찾으려면 먼저 중국의 힘이 어디서 나오는지 살펴봐야 한다. 중국 교육부는 올해 대학 졸업생이 1270만명이라고 밝혔다. 해마다 기록을 새로 쓰는 숫자다. 대학원에 새로 들어가는 사람도 한 해 석사 130만명, 박사 15만명 안팎이다. 작년 우리나라 4년제 대학 입학생은 33만명이고, 전문대를 합쳐도 50만명에 못 미친다. 중국은 광주광역시 인구만큼의 석·박사를 해마다 길러내고 있다. 양만 많은 것은 아니다. 우수 논문을 세는 네이처 인덱스에서 세계 상위 10개 기관 가운데 8곳이 중국이다. 응용과학 분야는 상위 31곳이 모두 중국 기관이다. 미국에서 일하는 최상위 AI 연구자 10명 중 4명이 중국 대학 출신이라는 조사도 있다. 중국은 5년마다 국가발전계획을 세우고 그대로 추진한다. 올해 시작한 15차 5개년 계획도 AI와 로봇을 맨 앞에 두었다. 뇌와 컴퓨터를 잇는 뇌컴퓨터인터페이스(BCI) 수술도 국가가 위험을 감수하고 해보라고 독려한다. 14억명 내수 시장은 그 자체로 시험장이다. 사람의 손발 움직임을 찍어 로봇을 가르치는 데이터도 이곳에서 가장 싸고 빠르게 모인다. 중국 청년들의 도전은 거칠다. 클로드 같은 미국 AI의 답을 대량으로 받아 자기 모델을 가르치는 증류 기법도 서슴없이 사용한다. 우리도 그런 시절이 있었다. 남의 제품을 뜯어 거꾸로 설계하며 기술을 익혔다. 옳은 방법은 아니었지만 배가 고팠기에 가능한 무모함이었다. 소득이 오르면서 그 배짱은 옅어졌다. 중국의 1인당 소득은 아직 우리의 3분의 1 수준이다. 가난이 키운 도전 정신이 중국 곳곳에 살아 있다. 이제 우리 숫자를 살펴볼 필요가 있다. 올해 초등학교 1학년은 29만명이고, 2031년에는 22만명으로 줄어든다. 대학은 4년 새 10곳이 문을 닫아 403곳이 남았다. 그 와중에 뛰어난 인재들은 미국으로 떠나고 있다. 첨단 학과를 만들어도 채울 학생이 없고, 연구실은 대학원생을 못 구해 과제를 반납하고 있다. 국내 인구만으로는 이 흐름을 되돌릴 수 없다. 그렇다고 주저앉을 이유는 없다. 지금 한국에 필요한 도전은 문을 여는 일이다. 아시아의 젊은 인재를 불러와 우리 사람으로 만들어야 한다. 문은 이미 열려 있다. 올해 국내 외국인 유학생은 30만7000명으로 처음 30만명을 넘어섰다. 베트남이 9만7000명으로 처음 중국을 앞섰고, 중국, 우즈베키스탄, 네팔, 몽골이 뒤를 잇는다. 한류에 끌려 한국을 찾은 청년들이다. 문제는 이들을 붙잡아 둘 제도다. 유학 비자 문턱을 낮추고, 공부하고 머물 수 있는 기간을 늘려야 한다. 학업 중 일할 수 있는 시간도 확대해야 한다. 졸업 뒤 구직 비자에서 취업 비자로 넘어가는 길을 열어야 한다. 미국은 유학생으로 실리콘밸리를 채웠다. 이들이 남으면 청년층 소비가 늘고 지방 대학이 버틸 수 있다. 모자란 연구 인력도 이들이 채울 수 있다. 미·중 정상이 무엇을 합의하든 한국의 숙제는 그대로다. 중국에서는 배고픈 청년들이 위험을 거칠게 무릅쓰고, 국가가 그 도전을 지원한다. 우리는 한류에 끌린 세계의 젊은이를 안으로 불러들이는 배짱을 내야 한다. 한국이 쌓아 온 인프라 위에서 이들과 함께 중국의 첨단 연구 인해전술에 맞서야 한다. 앞으로 10여년 동안 한국이 선택할 수 있는 가장 확실한 대중국 전략이다. AI도 지능이지만, 인간의 뇌는 여전히 상당 기간 AI를 오케스트레이팅할 수 있는 더 확실한 지능으로 남을 것이기 때문이다. 김경진 전 국회의원 2016kimkj@gmail.com

https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-new.p1: SIX AMERICAN presidents have tried to deal with North Korea’s nuclear weapons programme. Six have failed. Donald Trump would like another shot: he has said he expects to meet Kim Jong Un, North Korea’s dictator, this year. A planned trip to Asia for an APEC summit in November might provide an opening; Mr Trump’s former chief envoy to North Korea said in a recent speech he may even propose meeting in Pyongyang, where no sitting American president has ever been. Yet Mr Kim has made it clear that he will only meet if America drops its longstanding demands for “denuclearisation”, diplospeak for dismantling or removing his regime’s most potent weapons. Just one month after Mr Trump curtailed long-planned military exercises with South Korea in the hopes of rekindling his bromance with Mr Kim, the North Korean dictator, flanked by his teenage daughter , oversaw the test of a new purportedly hypersonic missile. The weapons would be an “incurable headache” for the country’s enemies, he crowed.
https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-new.p2: Mr Kim’s intransigence reflects a newfound confidence. For decades, America and its allies, together with China and Russia, tried to pressure North Korea to abandon its quest for the bomb. Despite those efforts, Mr Kim now possesses dozens of nuclear warheads , as well as missiles capable of carrying them to targets as far away as mainland America. A renewed alliance with Russia , forged on the battlefields in Ukraine, has given Mr Kim economic and diplomatic breathing room. Principled opposition to a nuclear-armed North Korea is eroding. Russia openly accepts North Korea’s nuclear status, with its foreign minister calling it a “closed issue”; China has fallen silent on the issue . South Korea’s left-wing president, Lee Jae Myung, now proposes leaving denuclearisation as an aspirational future goal. Mr Trump may be tempted to follow suit. https://www.bankingnews.gr/diethni/artic.title: North Korean soldiers transferred from Ukraine to South Korea – Seoul demands an apology from Zelensky
https://www.bankingnews.gr/diethni/artic.p1: A thriller is in full swing involving the two North Korean soldiers captured while fighting for Russia against Ukraine , who have now arrived in South Korea, raising questions regarding how they will be interrogated, protected, and resettled, as well as the legal basis of their transfer. The case has sparked a diplomatic incident between South Korea and Ukraine, with Seoul demanding that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky issue an apology, as he publicly revealed the fate of the soldiers from the podium of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York. The two soldiers are expected to undergo interrogation and security screening before South Korean authorities decide whether to grant them protection and initiate their resettlement process. According to Reuters, South Korea's Ministry of Unification stated on Monday that their cases will be examined under relevant legislation and past practice , meaning that the Act on the Protection and Settlement Support of North Korean Refugees may be applied. Under this law, the National Intelligence Service (NIS) interrogates North Koreans arriving in the country while holding them under temporary protective custody. Authorities can verify their identity, the circumstances under which they left North Korea , as well as any security-related matters. The investigation and temporary protection process can last up to 90 days and may be extended when deemed necessary. The military background of the two men, alongside their knowledge regarding the North Korean troop deployment in Russia, may lead to more extensive interrogations. South Korean opposition lawmaker Yu Yong-weon, who met with the soldiers in Ukraine in February 2025 , stated that they had served in North Korea's special forces and could provide information on Pyongyang's military training, capabilities, and involvement in the war. Those who receive protection typically attend a resettlement training program before integrating into South Korean society.
https://www.bankingnews.gr/diethni/artic.p2: South Korea's Minister of Unification typically decides whether a North Korean arriving in the country meets the criteria for state protection , although the director of the National Intelligence Service can make the determination for national security reasons. The sensitivity of the case may also keep the two soldiers out of the public spotlight for a longer duration compared to other North Koreans arriving in the country. Their physical and psychological condition is also expected to be evaluated . Yu stated that when he met with the soldiers in Ukraine, they were being held separately in a Ukrainian detention facility . As he noted, prolonged isolation and uncertainty may have affected their condition.

http://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/28/.title: Seoul seeks apology after Ukraine reveals transfer of North Korean POWs | The Peninsula Qatar
http://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/28/.p1: President of South Korea Lee Jae Myung speaks during the 81st session of the United Nations (U.N.) General Assembly at U.N. Headquarters on September 22, 2026 in New York City. Photo by RYAN MURPHY / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / GETTY IMAGES VIA AFP
http://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/28/.p2: Seoul: The Republic of Korea's presidential office has demanded an apology from Ukraine for denying an agreement to keep the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul confidential. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky disclosed last week that his country had sent two North Korean soldiers to the South, saying they were "not easy to capture alive". The intensifying dispute risks complicating Kyiv's efforts to obtain weapons from allies including Republic of Korea to fight off bombardments from Russia. Hours after Zelensky's remarks at the United Nations, Republic of Korea's President Lee Jae Myung expressed his dismay. "I do not know why the Ukrainian side broke the agreement and made the matter public, but it is very disappointing," he wrote on X. Seoul said confidentiality was key to protect the POWs' relatives from any repercussions in North Korea. "The families left behind in the North could face severe punishment," Cho Seong-ryoul, a former policy adviser to the presidential national security office, told AFP. Seoul's foreign ministry, in a statement to AFP on Monday, said that "as the matter concerns the personal safety of the individuals involved and their families, the two sides had agreed to handle it confidentially". Zelensky's aide Dmytro Lytvyn sought to play down the disclosure, saying that the president did not share any personal details. Ukraine is an "open country" and it would be unusual to hand over the prisoners in secret, he added. But Seoul condemned what it viewed as a breach of trust, noting that Zelensky's press office had denied there was a confidentiality agreement. That "false statement... seriously undermines trust between the two governments and gravely damages friendly relations between the two countries", said Seong Ghi-hong, senior presidential secretary for public relations. The presidential office of the Republic of Korea demands "an official explanation and apology", Seong said in a statement late Sunday, adding that Seoul was "considering additional measures that may be necessary regarding this matter". 'Backlash' Ukraine captured the two North Korean soldiers early last year among Pyongyang's troops fighting for Moscow. One of them told the Republic of Korea media he was conscripted aged 17 and had served in a reconnaissance unit. A lawmaker from the Republic of Korea had previously said the pair wanted to live a "normal life" in the South. Park Won-gon, a professor at Ewha Womans University in Seoul, said Kyiv's disclosure may have sparked concern that it could feed into Pyongyang's hostility towards South Korea. Since taking power in June 2025, Lee has reversed the stance of his hawkish predecessor Yoon Suk Yeol, offering nuclear-armed Pyongyang talks without preconditions. The Republic of Korea president "appears to be taking a 'low-key' approach as he is mindful of a possible backlash from North Korea," said Park. "North Korea has been using the deployed soldiers to create a heroic narrative for regime propaganda, and the South Korean government appears concerned that confirming the prisoners' return to the South and publicising it could further fuel hostility towards Seoul," he said. Beyond the ramifications within Seoul, the row also risks complicating Kyiv's requests to the ally for armaments supplies. Republic of Korea has so far not provided lethal weapons to Ukraine, citing a domestic ban on militarily aiding countries at war. Nevertheless, it had been considering requests for defensive weapons, especially since North Korea deployed troops to support Russia. The incident "has dealt a significant blow to the relationship of trust between Republic of Korea and Ukraine," Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University, told AFP.

https://www.naturalnews.com/2026-09-29-r.p1: Key points: Zelensky says North Koreans are being selected for training and deployment to Russia, adding to those already fighting. Putin's latest decree lifts the army to 1.55 million active servicemen, the fourth authorized increase in seven months. Pyongyang has supplied millions of artillery rounds, ballistic missiles and rocket systems, plus thousands of troops and laborers. North Korea's payoff includes food, energy, cash, drone know-how and possible advanced weapons technology. Pyongyang denies claims of tens of thousands more troops, and Ukrainian intelligence says the soldiers may serve in rear areas. Tension between Seoul and Kyiv over two captured North Korean soldiers shows how the alliance strains Russia's opponents. The bargain behind the deployment Zelensky, citing "new data" in a post on X, said North Koreans were "being selected for training and subsequent deployment to Russia." The claim landed the same Monday that Putin signed a decree raising the army's authorized strength to 1.55 million active servicemen and lifting the overall force to 2.4 million. The decree gives no reason, but the arithmetic speaks plainly. Meduza reports that it is the fourth increase in seven months, and together they added 52,500 defense personnel. An army that keeps raising its own ceiling is bleeding faster than it can recruit. Pyongyang's role is no novelty. Putin and Kim Jong Un confirmed for the first time that North Korean troops had been sent to Russia, and both leaders called them "heroes." Ukrainian and South Korean estimates put the total at 14,000 to 15,000 since 2024, mostly in Kursk, where they helped repel Ukraine's incursion. The Council on Foreign Relations notes that North Korea began shipping weapons in August 2023, long before its soldiers arrived, and later sent thousands of laborers and combat engineers. CSIS estimates that Pyongyang has transferred more than 15 million artillery shells. So why would Kim feed his soldiers into a foreign meat grinder? The official answer is treaty obligation. North Korea's Central Military Commission said Kim ordered combat troops abroad under the mutual defense treaty he signed with Putin in June 2024. The real answer is transactional. Analysts at CSIS describe a marriage of convenience, with Russia craving ammunition and North Korea craving food, energy and military technology. Kyiv and Seoul say the troops were sent in return for economic and military technology assistance. Another analysis describes a largely unofficial stream of Russian food, energy, cash and military technology flowing to Pyongyang as compensation. North Korea confirms it sent troops to Russia to support its war against Ukraine Consider what Kim gains in this situation. His army, untested in a major war since the Korean War, receives live combat education. His drone program, once stuck with outdated reconnaissance technology, has advanced rapidly thanks to the war. The EU, the United States and South Korea have voiced concern over the possible transfer of nuclear or ballistic missile-related technology, the crown jewels of any hermit regime. And with Moscow holding a Security Council veto, Kim gains a shield against the sanctions that once squeezed him. Ukrainian intelligence suggests the North Korean troops will reinforce Russia's rear positions, freeing Russian soldiers for assaults inside Ukraine. That is expansion by substitution: every North Korean guarding a rear area releases a Russian rifle toward the front. Ukraine has also claimed that North Korean troops based in Russia are operating reconnaissance drones across the border. The alliance also exposes fractures among Russia's opponents. Seoul announced a $100 million aid package in July, excluding lethal weapons, and now demands an apology from Kyiv after Zelensky disclosed at the UN General Assembly that Ukraine had transferred two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea. Seoul says confidentiality was necessary to protect the men and their relatives in the North. Kyiv says no secrecy agreement existed. Their cases will likely be reviewed under the North Korean Defectors Protection and Settlement Support Act, and questions about the legal basis of the transfer linger. The official story insists that Russia is isolated, bleeding and out of options. The evidence suggests a regime that has simply shopped for new partners. Ukraine's war is no longer a border dispute. It is a rehearsal for a larger contest; the tidy narrative of Russian isolationÂ continues to be debunked as Russia expands its military and economic coalitions. http://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/29/.title: North Korean DMZ landmine blasts 'violation of armistice': Seoul | The Peninsula Qatar
http://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/29/.p1: Defence Minister of the Republic of Korea Kang Shin-chul (L) speaks during a parliamentary defence committee hearing on the landmine explosion accident in the DMZ, at the National Assembly in Seoul on September 29, 2026. Photo by - / YONHAP / AFP
http://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/29/.p2: Seoul: The blasts that wounded three soldiers from the Republic of Korea last week were apparently caused by North Korean mines, Seoul said Tuesday, accusing Pyongyang of an armistice violation and warning of "corresponding measures". One soldier lost a foot due to the explosions in the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ), the heavily mined buffer zone that has divided the two Koreas since their 1953 armistice. The northern and southern boundaries of the zone are among the world's most heavily fortified frontiers and landmine incidents have previously heightened tensions between the two Koreas, which remain technically at war. Defence Minister of the Republic of Korea Kang Shin-chul spoke before a parliamentary hearing a day after his ministry said North Korean mines were "highly suspected" of causing the two explosions last week. "This is a clear violation of the armistice agreement, and since North Korea bears responsibility, we will take corresponding measures," he said. The military "has a range of necessary measures at our disposal, and we will implement them in stages", he added, without giving details. The minister said that dense vegetation in the area had hampered the work of mine detectors, and that forces from the Republic of Korea were in the DMZ to clear the area in advance of an operation with the UN Command. That operation would assess terrain changes caused by North Korean forces south of the Military Demarcation Line, which marks the nations' effective border. Hong Sung-pyo, senior researcher at the Seoul-based Korea Institute for Military Affairs, said it was reasonable to conclude that the mines were North Korean. "In practical terms, the only forces operating in the DMZ area are the South Korean, US and North Korean militaries," he told AFP. "Given the interoperability between South Korean and US forces, there would be little reason for the US military to have laid any mines there." Yang Jin-hyeok of the Joint Chiefs of Staff told lawmakers that a site investigation on Tuesday discovered an unexploded North Korean plastic anti-personnel mine. Seoul and Pyongyang remain technically at war since the Korean conflict ended in a truce, not a peace treaty. 'Few options' Since 2024, after North Korean leader Kim Jong Un designated Republic of Korea as his country's "principal enemy", Pyongyang's military has laid mines and built anti-tank barriers along the frontier as part of efforts to permanently seal it off. During the operation, Pyongyang also blew up the northern parts of inter-Korean roads no longer in use. Minister Kang said Tuesday that the North Korean mines linked to the September 21 incident were believed to have been laid as part of Pyongyang's border fortification work. There was no mention of last week's blasts on North Korean state media. In a 2015 incident, two soldiers from the Republic of Korea were seriously wounded in a landmine blast on the southern side of the DMZ, with one losing both legs. Seoul concluded that North Korean troops had crossed the Military Demarcation Line to plant the mines, an accusation Pyongyang denied. The incident prompted the Republic of Korea to resume anti-Pyongyang loudspeaker broadcasts along the border. But Yang Moo-jin, former president of the University of North Korean Studies in Seoul, said that there is "very little South Korea can realistically do" in retaliation for the latest blasts. "Resuming loudspeaker broadcasts would do more harm than good, particularly because residents in border areas would bear much of the disruption," he told AFP. "That effectively leaves Seoul with few options beyond demanding an apology from North Korea and seeking assurances that such an incident will not happen again" -- unless it is willing to risk heightened military tensions and further escalation, he added.

https://mignews.com/news/politic/seul-pe.title: Сеул перешел к открытой критике Киева из-за скандала с пленными КНДР - Guardian | MigNews - Новости Израиля и Мира на русском языке
https://mignews.com/news/politic/seul-pe.p2: Скандал вокруг двух северокорейских военнопленных превратил осторожную поддержку Украины со стороны Сеула в открытую критику. Об этом 29 сентября написало издание The Guardian в развернутой статье, посвященной дипломатическому скандалу между Украиной и Южной Кореей в связи с разглашением информации о передаче двух северокорейских военнопленных. Анализируя последствия конфликта, издание отмечает, что после того как Россия начала полномасштабное вторжение в Украину, Сеул осудил действия Москвы, присоединился к западным санкциям и в июле пообещал предоставить пакет поддержки в размере 100 миллионов долларов. В то же время страна дистанцировалась от боевых действий, отвергая прямую военную помощь Киеву, следуя своей практике не поставлять летальное оружие странам, находящимся в состоянии войны. До полномасштабного вторжения Россия являлась одним из крупнейших торговых партнеров Южной Кореи. Правительство Ли Чжэ Мена также стремится к тому, чтобы улучшить отношения с Пхеньяном, отметило The Guardian. Конфликт из-за пленных северокорейцев превратил осторожную поддержку Киева в открытую критику - в основном со стороны соратников Ли. Так, Ким Бен Чжу, депутат от Демократической партии, заявил, что нет «ни причин, ни необходимости» поддерживать Украину. Он также призвал правительство «немедленно» пересмотреть вопрос оказания помощи. 23 сентября президент Украины Владимир Зеленский во время Генеральной Ассамблеи ООН заявил, что украинская сторона передала Южной Корее двух военнопленных из КНДР. Он сообщил, что передача двух военнопленных состоялась недавно. 24 сентября президент Южной Кореи Ли Чжэ Мен обвинил Украину в нарушении договоренности о неразглашении после того, как Киев сообщил о передаче Сеулу двух северокорейских военнопленных. Он заявил, что вопрос их репатриации является «чрезвычайно чувствительным» и «связанным с дипломатией и национальной безопасностью». Позже украинские СМИ со ссылкой на источник в Офисе президента сообщили, что украинская сторона отрицает существование соглашения о конфиденциальности с Сеулом. Южнокорейская администрация заявила, что такое отрицание «серьезно подрывает» взаимное доверие и наносит ущерб дружественным отношениям между странами. По заявлению Сеула, украинское правительство само настаивало на конфиденциальности передачи, опасаясь внутренней критики из-за упущенной возможности обменять северокорейских военнопленных на украинских. Сеул согласился на конфиденциальность, принимая во внимание безопасность военнопленных и их семей, а также вопросы дипломатии и безопасности. В то же время представитель администрации президента Южной Кореи заявил, что Зеленский обнародовал информацию о передаче без предварительных разъяснений или консультаций, несмотря на наличие - по утверждению Сеула - взаимной договоренности. Издание Korea JoongAng Daily со ссылкой на высокопоставленного представителя администрации президента Южной Кореи сообщило, что Украина заранее уведомила Южную Корею о планах президента Владимира Зеленского упомянуть двух военнопленных из КНДР во время выступления на Генеральной Ассамблее ООН, несмотря на предварительную договоренность этого не делать. По его словам, украинская сторона уведомила Сеул по дипломатическим каналам и попросила отнестись к этому с пониманием.

https://www.chronicle.lu/category/intern.title: South Korea Made No Military Aid Pledge to Ukraine Over Transfer of North Koreans, Lawmaker Says
https://www.chronicle.lu/category/intern.p1: Published on Wednesday, 30 Sep 2026 09:13 by EO
https://www.chronicle.lu/category/intern.p2: SEOUL (Reuters) - South Korea made no promise to provide military support for Ukraine's fight against Russia in the transfer of two captured North Korean soldiers, a South Korean lawmaker said on Wednesday 30 September 2026, citing the country's intelligence agency. Ukraine imposed no preconditions on the transfer of the pair captured during fighting in Russia's Kursk region, Yoo Yeong-ha, a lawmaker from the opposition People Power Party, told reporters after a briefing by South Korea's National Intelligence Service (NIS). Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told the UN General Assembly last week that Ukraine had transferred two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea. After Zelensky disclosed the transfer, South Korea's presidential office demanded an official explanation and apology from Ukraine and accused Kyiv of violating an agreement to keep the move confidential to protect the soldiers and their relatives in North Korea. Ukraine has not apologised or expressed regret over the disclosure so far, Yoo said, citing the NIS. Kyiv has said no secrecy agreement existed. The soldiers are expected to undergo questioning and security screening before the South Korean authorities decide whether to grant them protection and begin the resettlement process. Under South Korean law, the NIS investigates applicants in temporary protective custody, verifying their identities, reasons for leaving North Korea and security-related concerns. Major arms producer According to Yoo, Zelensky may have announced the transfer of the North Koreans because he had hoped it would spur public support in South Korea for providing weapons and other aid to Ukraine. Ukraine's embassy in Seoul did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. South Korea, which is a major arms producer, has faced pressure from some Western countries and Kyiv to provide Ukraine with lethal weapons but has so far focused on non-lethal aid, including demining equipment. The soldiers were transferred to South Korea in mid-September, said another lawmaker, Youn Kun-young, who was also briefed by the NIS. The lawmaker said the pair had no health issues. Zelensky said in a post on X this week that more than 8,000 North Korean troops were on Russian territory and preparations were underway to deploy a further 10,000 troops. The Ukrainian president said in August as many as 50,000 North Korean soldiers could be sent to fight for Russia, and called on South Korea to provide support for Ukraine's air defence.
